skill.name: docs-review
skill.description: Review Metabase Markdown documentation changes for style, clarity, links, examples, and PR-ready numbered feedback.
skill.summary: Review Metabase documentation changes against the project style guide.
skill.author: metabase

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks and GitHub MCP tool names. The fixed shared style-guide include is not arbitrary traversal, but the skill does grant unnecessary Bash access for a docs review workflow.

remediation.issue: Bash is listed in allowed-tools even though the review workflow does not require shell commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove Bash from allowed-tools, or document the exact safe commands required for review.

remediation.issue: The skill imports a shared style guide with a parent-directory reference.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the style guide with the skill, or use a package-relative include that cannot reach unrelated parent files.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Bash Tool Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill declares Bash in allowed-tools, but the documented review workflow only needs file reads and GitHub review tools. This unnecessarily permits shell command execution during a documentation review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools declaration is explicit, and no later instruction requires Bash. The risk is permission exposure rather than evidence of malicious command use.

content.value_statement: Documentation reviewers need consistent feedback that matches Metabase style. This skill checks docs changes and returns focused, numbered issues for local review or GitHub PRs.
actual_capabilities: Checks Metabase documentation changes against the project writing style guide.
Flags tone, voice, structure, clarity, link, formatting, and example issues.
Formats feedback as sequentially numbered issues for easy discussion.
Supports local review output when GitHub MCP tools are unavailable.
Can prepare GitHub pending review comments when MCP tools are available.
Focuses on issues that materially improve reader experience.
limitations: It is tailored to Metabase documentation, not general editorial standards.
It relies on the files or diffs provided in the current context.
It cannot verify product behavior outside visible examples and commands.
GitHub PR posting requires compatible GitHub MCP tools.

use_cases.title: Review a documentation pull request
use_cases.description: Check changed Markdown files before merge and return concise comments that follow Metabase style.

use_cases.title: Polish feature documentation
use_cases.description: Find unclear language, weak headings, and style-guide issues before requesting formal review.

use_cases.title: Standardize release notes or guides
use_cases.description: Apply the same tone, link, formatting, and example checks across related documentation updates.

prompt_templates.title: Review one file
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Metabase documentation file for style-guide issues. Return only numbered issues that would materially help readers.

prompt_templates.title: Review a diff
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this documentation diff against Metabase style. Include line references, brief issue titles, and suggested fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on reader clarity
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these docs changes for structure, headings, tone, links, examples, and reader clarity. Skip minor preferences.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare PR comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Use PR review mode if GitHub MCP tools are available. Create sequential review comments for every material documentation issue.

output_examples.input: A changed setup guide uses formal language and a vague heading.
output_examples.output: Issue 1: Formal tone. Line 15 could use more direct language. Suggested fix: replace formal phrasing with plain wording.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds links with the text here and read more here.
output_examples.output: Issue 1: Descriptive link text. Replace vague link text with the destination or action, so readers understand the link target.

output_examples.input: A tutorial includes commands out of order and a full-screen screenshot.
output_examples.output: Issue 1: Command order. Put commands in execution order. Issue 2: Screenshot scope. Show only the relevant interface area.

best_practices: Provide the relevant Markdown file or pull request diff before asking for review.
Ask for material issues only, so feedback stays useful and concise.
Review the numbered comments before posting them to a public pull request.
anti_patterns: Do not use it as a general grammar checker for unrelated documentation styles.
Do not ask it to approve product facts that are not visible in the provided context.
Do not post generated review comments without checking tone and accuracy.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews Metabase documentation changes for style, clarity, formatting, links, examples, and reader value.

faq.question: Can it comment directly on GitHub pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes, when the required GitHub MCP review tools are available in the environment.

faq.question: Does it replace a human documentation reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It prepares focused feedback, but a reviewer should confirm accuracy and priority.

faq.question: Can I use it outside Metabase?
faq.answer: You can, but its checks are based on Metabase style and may not fit other projects.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: A Markdown file, a focused diff, or a pull request with documentation changes works best.

faq.question: Why are issues numbered?
faq.answer: Numbered issues make feedback easy to discuss, fix, and verify during review.
